predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the island of Cyprus, infobox predecessor 'Theme of Cyprus'

successors.name: Republic of Venice
successors.text: the island of Cyprus ('Venetian Cyprus', the infobox successor)

ledger.x: 1192: the Lusignans take Cyprus and found the Kingdom of Cyprus after the Third Crusade.
ledger.cp: Knights Templar (Cyprus under the Knights Templar, 1191-1192; no dossier)

ledger.x: 1196: the Holy Roman Emperor approves the crown of Cyprus, turning Guy's lordship into a kingdom under Aimery (the dynasty table calls Guy 'Lord' and Aimery 'First king').
1361: the kingdom takes Antalya on the Anatolian coast.
1361: the kingdom takes Corycus on the Cilician coast.
1372: Genoa seizes the port of Famagusta.
1489: Queen Catherine Cornaro sells Cyprus to Venice and the kingdom ends.

wars.name: Richard I's conquest of Cyprus (Third Crusade)
wars.outcome: Richard I conquered the island in 1191, sold it to the Knights Templar for 100,000 bezants, and after the Templars were expelled in an Easter 1192 uprising offered it to Guy of Lusignan; the Kingdom of Cyprus dates from 1192.

wars.name: Genoese seizure of Famagusta
wars.outcome: 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa'; the infobox calls the kingdom a tributary state of Genoa 1372-1426 (citation needed).

wars.name: Mamluk campaigns against Cyprus
wars.outcome: The lead: 'The Mameluks then made the kingdom a tributary state in 1426'; the peasant-revolt paragraph mentions 'the capture of King Janus'.

certainty.note: The island's coast is its border, so the main shape is sharp.
